title: Async batch labeling client: concurrency, pages and archive
scenario: An asyncio client submits one batch job per shard to a mock tagging API, polls each job, reads its page-numbered results, archives it, and routes low-confidence labels to review. At most max_concurrency shards run at once. Test 3 is the token/cost summary.

verified.why_correct: It is the blocking urllib call that `send` runs in a worker thread via asyncio.to_thread. HTTP errors are caught and returned as Response objects with their status, headers and decoded body, so callers can check the status themselves.

Returning 0 for attempt 0 looks like it ignores the interval, but it only skips the wait before the first poll. Every later poll waits poll_interval_s, so there are exactly max_polls status calls spaced as rule 2 says.

bugs.title: Semaphore created but never acquired
bugs.old:
async with limit:
        return await process_shard(client, shard, items)
bugs.symptom: test_1_concurrency_limit fails: AssertionError: 5 not less than or equal to 2 (all five shards submit at once). Every result and summary value is still right.
bugs.why: run_all builds a Semaphore(max_concurrency) and passes it down, but run_shard never enters it, so gather starts all five shards at once and the server sees five submits in flight together.
hints: The server saw more than two submits at the same time. What is supposed to limit that?
Follow the `limit` object from run_all into run_shard.
Wrap the call in `async with limit:`.
probes: Why did every result still come out right without the limit?
Why does the semaphore have to cover the whole shard (submit to archive) and not just the submit call?

bugs.title: archive() coroutine never awaited
bugs.symptom: test_2_every_batch_archived fails: the server's archived list is [] instead of all five batch ids, and a RuntimeWarning "coroutine 'BatchClient.archive' was never awaited" appears on stderr.
bugs.why: Calling an async def without await only creates a coroutine object; it never runs, so no DELETE is sent. Python prints a 'coroutine ... was never awaited' RuntimeWarning when the object is garbage collected.
hints: The server never received a single DELETE. Look at stderr while the tests run.
probes: What does calling an async function without await actually return?
Why did nothing else in the run change?

bugs.title: Last results page never fetched
bugs.symptom: test_3_shard_s2_all_pages fails: R10 (the only result on S2's third page) has status missing with label/score None instead of labeled dog 0.86.
bugs.why: range's stop is exclusive, so pages 2..total_pages-1 are read and the last page is skipped. Only S2 has more than one page (7 results at page_size 3), so only R10 goes missing.
hints: Only R10 is missing, and it's the 7th result of S2. How many pages does S2 have?
Look at the loop that reads pages after the first.
probes: Why didn't any other shard lose results?
Which page numbers does the loop request for total_pages = 3, before and after the fix?

bugs.title: Score equal to the threshold sent to review
bugs.symptom: test_4_shard_s3_review_threshold fails: R12 (score exactly 0.7) is needs_review instead of labeled.
bugs.why: The spec labels any score >= review_threshold. With `>`, R12's score of exactly 0.7 is routed to review.
hints: R12 has a score of exactly 0.7. What does the spec say about that?
Look at the threshold comparison in classify.
probes: Why is R13 (0.69) needs_review both before and after the fix?
Is comparing floats with >= safe here? Where does 0.7 come from?

bugs.title: Request ids trimmed but not upper-cased
bugs.symptom: test_5_shard_s5 fails: the S5 rows contain `r17` with label unknown, score 0.0, status needs_review, and no `R17` entry.
bugs.why: `r17` is sent and reported as lower-case. The API doesn't recognise that id, so it returns label `unknown` with score 0.0, and the report key is `r17` instead of `R17`.
hints: S5 has an `r17` key and an `unknown` label. Look at that row in requests.csv.
Compare how request ids and shard ids are cleaned in the loader.
Use norm_id for the request id.
probes: Why did ` R03` in S1 come through fine?
Why did the mock answer `unknown` instead of an error?

bugs.title: Tokens rounded to whole thousands before pricing
bugs.symptom: test_6_cost fails: cost_usd is 0.18 instead of 0.1763. total_tokens (8815) still passes.
bugs.why: round(tokens / 1000) rounds 8.815 thousand tokens up to 9 before multiplying, so the cost is 0.18 instead of 0.1763. Rounding has to be the last step, at 4 decimals.
hints: Look at where rounding happens in the cost formula.
probes: How large could the error be per run with the old formula?
Why does total_tokens pass while cost_usd fails?

context_qa.a: It loads the config and requests.csv (`load_requests` returns shards and a list of skipped ids), creates a `BatchClient`, runs `asyncio.run(run_all(client, shards))`, then builds per-request rows with `request_rows` and the summary with `summarize`.

context_qa.q: How does run_all start the shards?
context_qa.a: It creates `asyncio.Semaphore(client.config.max_concurrency)`, builds one `run_shard(limit, client, shard, items)` coroutine per shard, and awaits `asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)`. Any exception becomes a `ShardOutcome` with status `error`.

context_qa.q: What does process_shard do, in order?
context_qa.a: submit → poll_until_done → (if completed) take `usage.total_tokens` and classify every item from `fetch_results` → archive → return the ShardOutcome.

context_qa.q: What does a results page look like from the mock server?
context_qa.a: `{"data": [{"id", "label", "score"}, ...], "page": N, "total_pages": T}`, with `limit` items per page in the order the inputs were submitted. Unknown ids get label `unknown`, score 0.0.

context_qa.q: What does the mock server record that tests can look at?
context_qa.a: `requests` (every call with method, path, query, auth header and body), `archived` (batch ids that got a DELETE), and `peak_inflight` (the most submit calls being handled at the same moment; each submit takes about 0.12 s).

context_qa.q: How are retries handled on submit?
context_qa.a: `BatchClient.submit` loops `max_retries + 1` times, sleeping `Retry-After` seconds after a 429/5xx response. A final status other than 201 raises `BatchError`.
In `load_requests`: after trimming, an empty text puts `(shard, id)` on the skipped list and the request is never sent. `request_rows` adds those as `skipped` rows.
